Admission Plasma Glucose Requirement
data.description: Plasma glucose level required at Day 1 of each period for admission/procedure to proceed; otherwise admission is rescheduled
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Hypoglycemia Induction Target (Insulin Infusion Stop)
data.description: Threshold plasma glucose at which the insulin infusion is stopped and study drug administration is triggered
data.text: The insulin infusion will be stopped once the PG level reaches <60 mg/dL and approximately 5 minutes later patients will be administered either 3 mg LY900018 or 1 mg IMG (GlucaGen). Insulin infusion is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL. -5 mins = stop insulin infusion.

data.name: During Hypoglycemia Induction Assessment Trigger
data.description: Plasma glucose threshold defining the 'during hypoglycemia induction' Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale time point
data.text: During hypoglycemia induction will be when PG ≤75 mg/dL.

data.name: Fasting Condition for Laboratory Samples
data.description: Fasting requirement for clinical lab samples in treatment periods; no fasting needed at screening or follow-up
data.text: At Periods 1 and 2, samples should be collected from patients who have fasted at least 8 hours before any study procedures. Patients do not need to fast for samples at screening or follow-up.

data.name: Safety Review Gate After First 6 Patients
data.description: Interim safety review condition gating dosing of remaining patients
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients (regardless of type of diabetes) are administered LY900018 in Period 2, and the remaining patients will be dosed after confirmation of the safety. The investigator and Lilly CRP or scientist will review available safety data, including AEs, SAEs, vital signs, ECGs, and safety laboratory tests, from these patients after they complete Period 2 Day 1. If no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure are noted, the remaining patients will be dosed.

data.name: Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration
data.description: Protocol-defined procedures to follow if the patient has an insufficient response to glucagon administration (rescue)
data.text: Procedures for Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Treatment-Emergent ADA Triggering Additional Follow-up
data.description: Immunogenicity-based condition requiring extended follow-up sampling
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up. Samples for immunogenicity should be collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline (ie, returns to within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Insulin Regimen Acceptability
data.description: Review of insulin regimen required before undergoing hypoglycemia induction procedure
data.text: Review patients' insulin regimens to confirm acceptability to undergo the procedure to induce hypoglycemia.

data.name: Discharge Criteria / Stability Before Discharge
data.description: Conditions for discharge from CRU after glucagon administration
data.text: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration. A patient may remain inpatient at the CRU at the discretion of the investigator. After completion of all PK sampling, patients will be provided a carbohydrate-rich meal. The investigator will ensure the patient's PG is stable. A prandial insulin dose will be administered if needed. All patients will receive a carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge.

data.name: Non-inferiority Decision Criterion
data.description: Primary analysis statistical success criterion
data.text: Non-inferiority of LY900018 will be declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI constructed on the difference in percentage (IMG - LY900018) is less than the NIM of 10%.

data.name: Enrollment/Completion Target Condition
data.description: Sample size and replacement condition
data.text: Seventy five patients may be enrolled in order to have at least 66 patients (at least 30 patients with T1DM and T2DM, respectively) complete both periods with evaluable primary outcome. If patients discontinue from the study before completion of both periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, the patient may be replaced. Replacement should not occur beyond 75 patients enrolled, if it is expected to have at least 66 patients complete the study.

data.name: FSH Testing Condition
data.description: Conditional assessment for female patients
data.text: FSH (Female patients only) - when needed to confirm postmenopausal status.

data.name: Additional Time Points by Agreement
data.description: Adaptive addition of assessment time points
data.text: Time points may be added for each period (Period 1 and Period 2) if warranted and agreed upon between Lilly and the investigator. A time-matched PK (glucagon) sample may be collected at the follow-up immunogenicity assessment(s) if warranted and agreed upon between both the investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Screening to Period 1 Transition
data.text: Patients will undergo a screening examination within 28 days prior to enrollment (Days -28 to -2). Patients meeting eligibility criteria are admitted to the CRU on Period 1 Day -1 and randomly assigned to a treatment sequence prior to study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1.

data.name: Randomization to Treatment Sequence
data.text: Prior to the study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1, patients will be randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (either LY900018 in Period 1 and IMG in Period 2, or vice versa).

data.name: Period 1 to Washout to Period 2 (Crossover) Transition
data.text: Patients will be administered a single dose in Periods 1 and 2, which will be separated by a washout period of 3 to 14 days; patients cross over to the alternate treatment in Period 2.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients will return for a follow-up visit 26 to 30 days (28±2 days) after the last study treatment.

data.name: Follow-up to Additional TE ADA Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up with immunogenicity samples every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Dosing Hold Pending Safety Review
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients are administered LY900018 in Period 2; the remaining patients will be dosed only after confirmation of safety (no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure).

data.name: Rescheduling of Admission for Out-of-Range Plasma Glucose
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Response to Glucagon
data.text: Procedures for Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration are to be followed (Section 9.2.4); after completion of PK sampling a carbohydrate-rich meal is provided and a prandial insulin dose administered if needed to ensure plasma glucose stability.

data.name: Discontinuation for Concurrent Study Enrollment
data.text: Patients will be discontinued for enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or enrollment in any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation for Medical, Safety, Regulatory or Other Reasons
data.text: Participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation by Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken. Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation by Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Management of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: If the sponsor or investigator identifies a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria and was inadvertently enrolled, a discussion must occur between the Lilly CP/CRP and the investigator to determine if the patient may continue in the study. If both agree it is medically appropriate to continue, the investigator must obtain documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP to allow the inadvertently enrolled patient to continue in the study with or without continued treatment with investigational product.

data.name: Study-Level Stopping Rule
data.text: Following the review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the Investigator and sponsor (Section 10.3.7).

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED) Visit
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow-up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities; the Follow-up/ED visit serves as the early discontinuation visit.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods (Period 1 and Period 2) with evaluable primary outcome and the follow-up visit performed within 28±2 days after the last study treatment.

data.name: Completion of TE ADA Follow-up
data.description: Additional immunogenicity follow-up ends when the ADA titer returns to baseline (within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or at 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow-up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site, after diligent attempts by site personnel.

data.name: Study Termination for Safety
data.description: The study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the Investigator and sponsor following review of safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1.

data.name: Discontinuation and Replacement
data.description: If patients discontinue from the study before completion of both periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, the patient may be replaced (replacement should not occur beyond 75 patients enrolled).

data.name: Admission Plasma Glucose Check
data.description: Decision on Day 1 of each period whether to proceed with the hypoglycemia induction procedure or reschedule admission based on PG 90 to 250 mg/dL.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop / Dosing Decision
data.description: Once bedside PG reaches <60 mg/dL, insulin infusion is stopped and approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision After First 6 Patients
data.description: After the first 6 patients complete Period 2 Day 1, the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist decide whether to dose the remaining patients or stop the study for safety.

data.name: Glucagon Response Assessment / Rescue Decision
data.description: Assessment of response to glucagon administration; insufficient response triggers protocol-specified rescue procedures.

data.name: TE ADA Follow-up Decision
data.description: At Follow-up/ED, patients with treatment-emergent ADA enter additional immunogenicity follow-up every 84±7 days.

data.name: Discharge Decision
data.description: At 6 hours after glucagon administration, the investigator decides whether to discharge the patient or keep them inpatient at the CRU.

data.name: Primary Non-inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: Final analysis decision based on the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI for the difference in treatment success percentage versus the 10% non-inferiority margin, requiring 66 completers.
